title: Your heart doesn't rest when you sleep 🫀 #shorts
desc:
You think your heart rests at night. It doesn't: it beats tens of thousands of times while you sleep, and over 100,000 times a day. A mouse's heart beats ~600 times a minute, a blue whale's can drop to just 2.

Math: 8 h × 60 bpm = 28,800 · 70 mL per beat ≈ 7,000 L a day.
Sources: American Heart Association; Cleveland Clinic; Goldbogen et al. 2019, PNAS (blue whale heart rate).

title: The 10% brain myth, in numbers 🧠 #shorts
desc:
No, you don't use only 10% of your brain. It has ~86 billion neurons, is ~2% of your weight but uses ~20% of your energy — about 20 watts.

Sources: Azevedo et al. 2009, J Comp Neurol; Raichle & Gusnard 2002, PNAS.

title: You're blind for up to 30 minutes a day 👁️ #shorts
desc:
Each blink lasts ~100–150 ms and you blink ~15 times a minute — up to half an hour of darkness a day. Your brain hides it from you. Reading drops your blink rate to ~4 a minute.

Sources: UCL (blink duration); Bentivoglio et al. 1997, Movement Disorders (blink rates); Volkmann et al. 1980 (blink suppression).

title: Your body makes 2 million blood cells every second 🩸 #shorts
desc:
Your bone marrow makes ~2 million new red blood cells every second (~170 billion a day). Each lives ~120 days, and ~25 trillion are circulating right now.

Sources: Stanford Blood Center; Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLOS Biology.

title: Your lungs are NOT two balloons 🫁 #shorts
desc:
You breathe ~20,000 times a day, moving 10,000+ liters of air into ~480 million tiny air sacs. Spread flat, that's ~70 m² — about 35× your skin.

Sources: Cleveland Clinic (breathing rate); Ochs et al. 2004, AJRCCM (alveoli count).

title: You're losing your skin right now #shorts
desc:
Your skin is your heaviest organ (~3.6 kg) and you shed ~30,000–40,000 skin cells every minute. New cells take 2–4 weeks to climb to the surface.

Sources: Cleveland Clinic; KidsHealth (Nemours).

title: Why babies have more bones than you 🦴 #shorts
desc:
Newborns have ~270–300 bones; many fuse as we grow, leaving adults with 206. More than half (106) are in your hands and feet.

Sources: Cleveland Clinic; Encyclopaedia Britannica.
